stem_book: State whether the following are true or false. (i) The degree of dissociation can never be greater than 1. (ii) Equilibrium vapour density can be used to estimate the degree of dissociation of solid substances. (iii) The degree of dissociation and equilibrium vapour density are inversely proportional. (iv) For a substance that is partially dissociated, the degree of dissociation is between 0 and 1. (v) Changes in temperature can affect both equilibrium vapour density and the degree of dissociation.
key: True α is a fraction of what was taken, so its ceiling is 1 | False the vapour-density method applies to gases, not solids | True as α rises the equilibrium vapour density falls | True partial dissociation means 0 < α < 1 | True temperature changes K, hence α, hence the vapour density
derived: (i) True (ii) False (iii) True (loosely; strictly D/d = 1+(n-1)α, not inverse proportion) (iv) True (v) True
correct_answer: (i) True (ii) False (iii) True (loosely; strictly D/d = 1+(n-1)α, not inverse proportion) (iv) True (v) True
reason: Five-part true/false recap with separate answers; manifest split it into 5 entries sharing one code. Part (iii) 'True' is only loose: d = D/[1+(n-1)α] falls as α rises but is not inversely proportional to α.
